title: Lottie Hack-Lazzari
text:
Research interests
I am interested in:

Quantitative mixed-coniferous and eucalypt forest ecology (structural, successional, and fire-regime dynamics)

Martian planetary science/geomorphology (crustal extension, fluvial incision, and slope failure) in Tharsis/Valles Marineris.

Quantitative remote sensing

title: Projects
text: Is it possible to find spatial correlation between slope-forced hydrological routing and grove-scale distribution of Monarch Sequoiadendron giganteum using study-relative low-resolution remote sensing in the form of a 1m DEM-derived TWI?

title: Projects
section: Analysing terrain-controlled mass wasting of Ius Chasma’s wall slopes
text:
Analysing terrain-controlled mass wasting of Ius Chasma’s wall slopes
Using >1.0m resolution HiRISE DEM’s, analysing slope, aspect, and curvature to find terrain controlled mass wasting events within Ius Chasma.

title: Experience
text:
Quantitative and Applied Ecology Research Group (QAEco)
University of Melbourne
April 2026

Supervised by Prof Peter Vesk.

Assisted with vegetation surveying and biomass data collection in mixed-species sclerophyll forest (Starvation Creek) and coastal grassland (Phillip Island Summerland Peninsula)
Assisted plant specimen collection and herbarium curation supporting functional trait analysis of Eucalyptus species
Contributed to seed viability estimation via x-ray imaging at the Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria herbarium
Received instruction in image processing for leaf morphology and canopy structure
Introduced to species distribution modelling
